transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We've got an inbound licensing request from an international airline looking to put our independent concert documentary on their passenger-entertainment system. The draft proposal on the table is for a worldwide, twelve-month, non-exclusive license using the current picture and delivery master. Before I can sign off on the final terms and delivery instructions, I need our rights, music, and post-production leads to report any approval conditions at this greenlight meeting. So let's walk through it — rights first, then music, then post. Any flags or conditions I need to be aware of?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Mara, I've got a significant flag on the rights side. I reviewed the executed performer agreements yesterday, and they only permit licensing of the documentary in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom — not worldwide — and only for a six-month non-exclusive term, not twelve months. Additionally, those agreements require a written rights amendment before we can proceed to delivery. The buyer's draft proposing worldwide, twelve-month terms exceeds what we're currently cleared for, so we'll need to either negotiate the buyer down to our authorized scope or secure amendments from the performers before I can greenlight this.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Mara, I have a music flag to report. I checked the publisher's clearance ledger this morning and confirmed that the current cut's use of the song 'Afterglow Avenue' lacks the synchronization clearance required for airline distribution. The cleared replacement is 'Night Transit,' and I have not yet updated the music cue sheet because the final territory and term were still unsettled. Once the rights situation Jonah just flagged gets resolved and we know the final territory and term, I'll need to update the cue sheet with the replacement track before delivery can proceed.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Mara, I've got a post-production flag. I completed the airline's ingest test with our delivery vendor today, and the confirmed delivery spec requires a 1080p SDR master with stereo Lt/Rt audio and English SDH captions delivered as a sidecar VTT file. Our current delivery master is 4K with a different audio and caption package, so it won't pass their ingest. I have not yet issued the revised export order because the licensing terms are still pending.
